name: cold-start-warmup-p5
prompt: how do I stop the first request after a deploy or a scale-up from being painfully slow

chunks.content: append every admin action to an immutable audit log
the very first product page after a cache flush is slow because nothing is cached yet, then it warms up
lazy-load below-the-fold images so the initial paint is lighter
scheduled a nightly vacuum to keep query plans fresh
outbound email is pushed to a background queue and sent by a worker
dark-launch the new ranking model to staff behind a flag
localize the date picker to the viewer's region
the first login feels slow because we deliberately use an expensive password hash to resist brute force
track time-to-first-successful-request per instance so we can see the cold penalty
report list uses cursor pagination on the last id
the worker drains the backlog queue oldest-first after a deploy
we keep a small floor of always-on instances so a scale-up event never routes users to a process that's booting from scratch
moved expensive client initialization out of the request path and into boot, so the first caller doesn't trigger lazy setup of the database and storage clients
decided that a freshly started instance hits its readiness probe only after it has primed the connection pool and pulled the hot config into memory, so the first real request isn't paying that cost
a startup hook fires a handful of synthetic requests against the heaviest routes to trigger JIT compilation and fill the local caches before traffic is routed in
